selection: attention-compression layer classes; all three classes present in every forward
provenance: Shapes from the live checkpoint config (hidden 4096, 64 heads, head_dim 512, num_key_value_heads 1, index_topk 512, sliding_window 128, compress_ratios) cross-checked against a rocprofv3 kernel trace on MI355X: the unified-KV prefill index/store kernels (_build_prefill_indices_kernel, _prefill_lengths_kernel, _swa_scatter_kernel, _init_compressed_attn_metadata_kernel) each fire 43 times, once per layer. Case counts are the compression partition: 21 C4, 20 C128, 2 ratio-0. NOT the routing partition.
geometry_aggregation_key: grid(x,y,z) + workgroup(x,y,z) + VGPR + Accum_VGPR + SGPR + LDS + Scratch

observed_geometry.note: rocprofv3 Grid_Size is WORK-ITEMS, not workgroups.
observed_geometry.companion_asm_path: On this image SGLANG_OPT_FLASHMLA_SPARSE_PREFILL is disabled by default on ROCm/HIP, so prefill attention math went to pa_prefill_16mx8_32nx1_kernel: 65536 work-items at wg=512 = 128 workgroups on 256 CUs, LDS 135168 B/WG (132 KB of gfx950's 160 KB), vgpr=128, scratch=108. Half the device idle and the occupied half at minimum occupancy.

physics: The Triton prefill path attends two KV sources in one pass. Its asm counterpart on this image is occupancy-walled: 132 KB LDS per workgroup allows one workgroup per CU, and the launch only covers 128 of 256 CUs. That LDS figure was predicted at ~136 KB from DeepSeek's own TileLang sparse_attn reference before being measured, so the pressure is intrinsic to the operator at h=64/d=512, not an artefact of a NVIDIA-tuned reference.
